daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Constitutional Court is holding a hearing today to deliver a ruling on the Military Justice Law, focusing on concerns about impunity for military personnel. The KPK arrested a BNPB official in a sting operation but released the Secretary General despite his involvement, with the KPK chief saying the head of BNPB will only be summoned if necessary. Separately, the Ministry of Home Affairs has dismissed Gowa Regent Husniah Talenrang with dishonor.

  • The Constitutional Court is delivering its ruling on the Military Justice Law today, addressing concerns about military impunity.
  • The KPK chairman explained the release of the Secretary General of BNPB despite being caught in the operation.
  • The KPK chairman said the BNPB head will not be summoned unless deemed necessary.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs dishonorably dismissed Husniah Talenrang as Regent of Gowa.
  • A witness testified that an extortion defendant was previously picked up by investigators at an entertainment venue.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Foreign Ministry criticized Israel's restrictions on Indonesian pilots as discriminatory after Israeli authorities barred an Indonesian pilot from entering the country aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight. Indonesia and Russia are seeking to deepen their defense cooperation. The Foreign Ministry also confirmed that two Indonesian nationals injured in the Houthi attack on Riyadh airport have recovered.

  • Indonesia called Israel's restrictions discriminatory and highlighted legal errors in the decision.
  • Indonesia and Russia are seeking to deepen their defense cooperation.
  • The Foreign Ministry reported that two Indonesians injured in the Riyadh airport attack have recovered.
  • Indonesia is looking to partner with Gabon on rare earth minerals development.
  • Indonesia will help build a cassava processing plant in Cameroon.

Other

PLN replaced its director amid the ongoing Batam electricity outage crisis, with the subsidiary now under direct control of state holding company Danantara. Pertamina Patra Niaga strengthened its fleet and extended terminal operations to 24 hours to accelerate fuel distribution amid widespread shortages. Separately, the National Human Rights Commission has launched an investigation into the human rights impact of the Kalimantan forest fires.

  • PLN changed its director amid the Batam power outage, with PLN Batam now directly under Danantara.
  • Pertamina Patra Niaga strengthened its fleet and extended terminal operations to accelerate fuel distribution.
  • The National Human Rights Commission is investigating the human rights impact of the Kalimantan wildfires.
  • The government's BGN program launched 980 MBG kitchens in remote and high-stunting regions.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs launched Safe Santri and an anti-violence task force for Islamic boarding schools.
  • Immigration non-tax revenue reached Rp 8.68 trillion, exceeding the 2026 target.
